questions.question: Let \(X_{1}\), \(X_{2}\)  be two independent normal random variables with means \(\mu 1\), \(\mu 2\) and standard deviations, respectively. Consider  \(Y=X_{1}-X_{2}\); \(\mu _{1} = \mu _{2}\)=1, \(\sigma _{1}=1, \sigma _{2}=2\). Then
options: Y is normally distributed with mean 0 and variance 1
Y is normally distributed with mean 0 and variance 5
Y has mean 0 and variance 5, but is NOT normally distributed
Y has mean 0 and variance 1, but is NOT normally distributed
questions.explanation:
\(\mu_{1}=1, \mu_{2}=1, \sigma_{1}=1, \sigma_{2}=2\)
\(x_{1} \text{ and } x_{2}\) are two independent random variables
\[\begin{aligned} Y &=X_{1}-X_{2} \\ \mu(Y) &=\mu\left(X_{1}-X_{2}\right) \\ &=\mu\left(X_{1}\right)-\mu\left(X_{2}\right)=\mu_{1}-\mu_{2}=1-1=0 \\ \text{Var}(Y) &=\text{Var}\left(X_{1}-X_{2}\right) \\ &=\text{Var}\left(X_{1}\right)+\text{Var}\left(X_{2}\right)-\text{Cov}\left(X_{1}, X_{2}\right) \end{aligned}\]
since \(X_{1} \text{ and }X_{2}\) are independent variables
\[\begin{aligned} \text{Var}(Y) &=\operatorname{Var}\left(X_{1}\right)+\operatorname{Var}\left(X_{2}\right) \\ &=\sigma_{1}^{2}+\sigma_{2}^{2}=1+4 \\ \operatorname{Var}(Y) &=5 \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: engineering-mathematics
questions.question: A six-faced fair dice is rolled five times. The probability (in %) of obtaining "ONE" at least four times is
questions.explanation:
A dice is rolled 5 times
\[\begin{aligned} n&=5 \\ P&=(\text { Probability of getting } 1)=\frac{1}{6} \\ q&=1-\frac{1}{6}=\frac{5}{6} \end{aligned}\]
Probability of getting 1 at least 4 times is
\[\begin{aligned} P(x \geq 4) &=P(x=4)+P(x=5) \\ &=^{n} C_{4} p^{4} q^{n-4}+^{n} C_{5} p^{5} q^{n-5} \\ &=^{5} C_{4} p^{4} q^{1}+^{5} C_{5} p^{5} q^{0} \\ &=5 \times\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)^{4}\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^{1}+1 \times\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)^{5} \times\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^{0}\\ &=\frac{25}{(6)^{5}}+\frac{1}{(6)^{5}}=\frac{26}{(6)^{5}}=0.0033 \end{aligned}\]
% probability =0.33%

questions.question:
F(z) is a function of the complex variable z = x + iy given by
\(F(z)=iz+kRe(z)+ i \; lm(z)\)
For what value of k will F(z) satisfy the Cauchy-Riemann equations?
questions.explanation: \[\begin{aligned} F(z) &=i z+k \operatorname{Re}(z)+i \operatorname{Im}(z) \\ u+i v &=i(x+i y)+k x+i y \\ u+i v &=k x-y+i(x+y) \\ u &=k x-y, v=x+y \\ u_{x} &=k, u_{y}=-1 \\ V &=x+y \\ v_{x} &=1 \\ v_{y} &=1 \\ u_{x} &=v_{y} \\ k &=1 \end{aligned}\]

questions.question: If \(f(z)=(x^{2}+ay^{2})+ibxy\)  is a complex analytic function of \(z=x+iy\) ,where \(i=\sqrt{-1}\), then

Given that the analytic function
\[\begin{aligned} f(2) &=\left(x^{2}+a y^{2}\right)+i b x y \\ u+i v &=\left(x^{2}+a y^{2}\right)+i(b x y) \\ u &=x^{2}+a y^{2} ; \quad v=b x y \\ u_{x} &=2 x ; \quad u_{y}=2 a y \\ v_{x} &=b y ; \quad v_{y}=b x \\ u_{x} &=v_{y} ; \quad u_{y}=-v_{x} \\ 2 x &=b x ; \quad 2 a y=-b y \\ b &=2 ; \quad 2 a=-b \quad \text { since } b=2 \\ 2 a &=-2 \\ a &=-1 \end{aligned}\]

questions.question: Consider the matrix \[A=\begin{bmatrix} 50 & 70\\ 70 & 80 \end{bmatrix}\]  whose eigenvectors  corresponding to eigenvalues \(\lambda _{1}\) and \(\lambda _{2}\) are \[X_{1}=\begin{bmatrix} 70\\ \lambda _{1}-50 \end{bmatrix}\] and \[X_{2}=\begin{bmatrix} \lambda _{2}-80\\ 70 \end{bmatrix}\] ,  respectively. The value of \(X_{1}^{T} X_{2}\)  is _____.

\[A=\left[\begin{array}{ll}50 & 70 \\70 & 80\end{array}\right]\]
Eigen values of A are \(\lambda_{1}, \lambda_{2}\)

\(y=\frac{2000}{3} \sin 3 x\)
\(\text{when }x=1 \quad y=\frac{2000}{3} \sin 3=94.08\)

By Gauss divergence theorem

\(= 2 V \text { where } V \text { is volume of } x ^ { 2 } + y ^ { 2 } + z ^ { 2 }\)
\(= 2 \left( \frac { 4 } { 3 } \pi ( 3 ) ^ { 3 } \right) = 226.08\)

\[\begin{aligned} \int_{c} \bar{F} \cdot \vec{r}\acute{} d x=\int_{c} \bar{F} \cdot & d \bar{r}=\int_{c} F_{1} d x+F_{2} d y \\ &=\iint_{R}\left(\frac{\partial F_{2}}{d x}-\frac{\partial F_{1}}{d y}\right) d x d y \end{aligned}\]
\[\begin{aligned} &\begin{array}{l} \begin{array}{rl} F_{1}=y & F_{2}=2 x \\ & =\iint_{R}(2-1) d x d y \end{array} \\ \begin{aligned} \frac{\partial F_{1}}{\partial y}=1 \quad \frac{\partial F_{2}}{\partial x} &=2 \\ &=\iint d x d y \end{aligned} \end{array}\\ &=\text { Area of the circle with radius } \frac{4}{\sqrt{\pi}}=\pi\left(\frac{4}{\sqrt{\pi}}\right)^{2}\\ &=\pi \frac{16}{\pi}=16 \end{aligned}\]

\(\text{rank} =2 \quad\) The equation are \(x_{2}=0\)
No. of variables \(=3 x_{3}=0\)

Only one independent Eigen vector in the case of
\(\lambda=2\)
Hence finally no. of L.I. Eigen vectors =2

\(\Rightarrow \quad C_{2}+4 C_{1} =1.5 \qquad ...(ii)\)

\(C_{2}=-0.5\)

\(y=\frac{e^{x}-e^{-x}}{2}\)

Assuming \(x_{0}=1 \quad\left(1 \text{ rad}=57.32^{\circ}\right)\)

Again,

\(=0.5425\)

questions.question: Consider two solutions \(x(t)=x_{1}(t)\) and  \(x(t)=x_{2}(t)\)  of the differential equation \(\frac{\mathrm{d}^2x(t)}{\mathrm{d} t^{2}}+x(t)=0,\; t\gt 0\)  , such that \(x_{1}(0)=1,\; \frac{\mathrm{d}x_{1}(t)}{\mathrm{d} t}|_{t=0} =0,x_{2}(0)=0,\frac{\mathrm{d}x_{2}(t)}{\mathrm{d} t}|_{t=0} =1\)  . The wronskian \[W(t)=\begin{vmatrix} x_{1}(t) & x_{2}(t)\\ \frac{\mathrm{d} x_{1}(t)}{\mathrm{d} t} & \frac{\mathrm{d} x_{2}(t)}{\mathrm{d} t} \end{vmatrix}\]  at \(t=\pi /2\)  is.
questions.explanation:
Given differential equation in symbolic form is
\(\left(D^{2}+1\right) x(t)=0\)
Its A.E. is \(D^{2}+1=0\)
\(\therefore \quad D=\pm i\)
So, C.F. is
\(x_{1}(t)=C_{1} \cos t\)
\(x_{2}(t)=C_{2} \sin t\)
\(\therefore x_{1}(0)=C_{1}=1\)
\[\begin{array}{l} \begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad x_{1}(t) &=\operatorname{cost} \\ \text { it satisfies }\left.\begin{matrix} \frac{\mathrm{d} x_{1}(t)}{d t}\end{matrix} \right|_{t=0} &=0 \end{aligned} \\ \qquad \begin{aligned} x_{2}(0) &=0=C_{2} \sin (0)\left(\because C_{2} \neq 0\right) \\ \frac{d x_{2}(t)}{d t} &=C_{2} \cos t \end{aligned} \\ \left.\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d x_{2}(t)}{d t}\right|_{t=0}=C_{2}=1 \end{array}\]
\[\begin{array}{l} \therefore \;\; x_{2}(t)=\sin t \\ W(t)= \begin{vmatrix} x_{1}(t) & x_{2}(t) \\ \frac{d x_{1}(t)}{d t} & \frac{d x_{2}(t)}{d t}\end{vmatrix}= \begin{vmatrix} \cos t & \sin t \\ -\sin t & \cos t \end{vmatrix} \\ M(t)=\cos ^{2} t+\sin ^{2} t=1 \end{array}\]

questions.question: An analytic function of a complex variable \(z=x+iy\)  is expressed as \(f(z)=u(x,y)+iv(x,y)\)  , where \(i=\sqrt{-1}\). If \(u(x,y)=x^{2}-y^{2}\), then expression for \(v(x,y)\)  in terms of x, y and a general constant c would be
questions.explanation:
As per Cauchy-Riemann equations:
\(\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=\frac{\partial v}{\partial y} and \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=-\frac{\partial v}{\partial x}\)
\(u=x^{2}-y^{2}\)
\(\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=2 x, \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=-2 y\)
\(\therefore \quad \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}=2 x\)
\(\Rightarrow \quad v=2 x y+f(x)\)
\(\frac{\partial v}{\partial x}=2 y+f(x)\)
\(\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=2 y+f^{\prime}(x)\)
\(\Rightarrow \quad f^{\prime}(x)=0 \quad \text { i.e. } f(x)=c\)
\(\therefore \quad v=2 x y+c\)

questions.question: One of the eigenvectors of the matrix  \[\begin{bmatrix} -5 & 2\\ -9 & 6 \end{bmatrix}\]  is
questions.explanation:
The characteristic equation \(| A-\lambda D=0\)
\[\text{i.e.} \left|\begin{array}{cc}-5-\lambda & 2 \\ -9 & 6-\lambda\end{array}\right|=0\]
\(\text{or } (\lambda-6)(\lambda+5)+18=0\)
\(\text{or } \quad \lambda^{2}-6 \lambda+5 \lambda-30+18=0\)
\(\text{or } \quad \lambda^{2}-\lambda-12=0\)
\(\text{or } \lambda=\frac{1 \pm \sqrt{1+48}}{2}=\frac{1 \pm 7}{2}=4,-3\)
Corresponding to \(\lambda=4,\) we have
\[\; [A-\lambda I] x=\left[\begin{array}{cc}-5-\lambda & 2 \\-9 & 6-\lambda\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}x \\y\end{array}\right]\]
\(=0\)
\[\text{Or, } \left[\begin{array}{ll}-9 & 2 \\ -9 & 2\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}x \\ y\end{array}\right]=0\]which gives only one independent equation,
\(-9 x+2 y=0\)
\(\therefore \frac{x}{2}=\frac{y}{9}\) gives eigen vector (2,9)
Corresponding to \(\lambda=-3,\)
\[=\left[\begin{array}{ll}-2 & 2 \\-9 & 9\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}x \\y \end{array}\right]=0\]
which gives -x+y=0 (only one independent equation)
\(\therefore \quad \frac{x}{1}=\frac{y}{1} \quad\) which gives (1,1)
So, the eigen vectors are \[\left\{\begin{array}{l}2 \\ 9\end{array}\right\} and \left\{\begin{array}{l}1 \\ 1\end{array}\right\}\]

 where k is a constant, subjected to the boundary conditions  u(0) = 0  and  u(L) = U,  is

We have \(\frac{\mathrm{d^{2}u} }{\mathrm{d} x^{2}}-k\frac{\mathrm{du} }{\mathrm{d} x}=0\)
\((D^2-kD)u=0\)
The auxiliary equation is
\[\begin{aligned} m^2-km&=0\\ m(m-k)&=0\\ m&=0,k \end{aligned}\]
Thus the complete solution is
\[\begin{aligned} u&=C_1e^{0x}+C_2e^{kx}\\ u&=C_1+C_2e^{kx} \end{aligned}\]
From given condition
\(u(0)=0:\;\; C_1+C_2=0 \;\;\;...(i)\)
\(u(L)=U:\;\; U=C_1+C_2e^{kL}\;\;\;...(ii)\)
Subtracting equation (i) from (ii), we get
\(U=C_2(e^{kL}-1)\)
\(C_2=\frac{U}{e^{kL}-1}\)
From equation (i), we have
\(C_1=-C_2=\frac{-U}{e^{kL}-1}\)
Substitute these values in the expression for u, we get
\(u=\frac{-U}{e^{kL}-1}+\frac{U}{e^{kL}-1}e^{kx}=U\left ( \frac{1-e^{kx}}{1-e^{kL}} \right )\)

questions.subject: engineering-mathematics
questions.question:
The probability that a student knows the correct answer to a multiple choice question is \(\frac{2}{3}\)
If the student does not know the answer, then the student guesses the answer. The probability of the guessed answer being correct is \(\frac{1}{4}\)
Given that the student has answered the question correctly, the 
conditional probability that the student knows the correct answer is
questions.explanation:
Let A be the event when student knows the answer and B be the event when student guesses the answer. Therefore
\(P(A)=P(A\cap B)=\frac{2}{3}\)
\(P(B)=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{3}\times \frac{1}{4}=\frac{9}{12}\)
where \(\frac{2}{3}\) is the probability of correct answer and \(\frac{1}{3}\) is the probability that student does not know the answer. So guesses the answer and probability of correct guess is \(\frac{1}{4}\). Therefore total probability of correct answer
\(=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{1}{4}=\frac{9}{12}\)
Conditional probability that student knows the correct answer
\(P(A/B)=\frac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}=\frac{\frac{2}{3}}{\frac{9}{12}}=\frac{8}{9}\)

 with the boundary conditions of y(0) =0 and  y(1) = 1. The complete solution of the differential equation is
questions.explanation:
\(x^{2} \frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}+x \frac{d y}{d x}-4 y =0\)
\(y(0)=0 \text { and } y(1)=1\)
Choice (A) satisfies the initial condition as well as equation as shown below:
\(\text { If } \quad y=x^{2}\)
\(\Rightarrow \quad y(0)=0^{2}=0 \text { and } y(1)=1^{2}=1\)
\(\text{Also,} \quad \frac{d y}{d x}=2 x\)

\(\Rightarrow x^{2} \frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}+x \frac{d y}{d x}-4 y=x^{2} \times 2+x \times 2 x-4 \times x^{2}\)
\(=2 x^{2}+2 x^{2}-4 x^{2}=0\)
So \(\qquad y=x^{2}\) is the solution to this equation with given boundary conditions.

Which is only one equation,

Whose solution is

\[=\frac{1}{\sqrt{(-k)^{2}+\left(k^{2}\right)}}\left[\begin{array}{c}-k \\k\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{c}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{array}\right]\]

since \(2-3 x\) and \(3 x-2\) are polynomials, these are continuous at all points. The only concern is at
\(x=\frac{2}{3}\)
Left limit at \(x=\frac{2}{3} is 2-3 \times \frac{2}{3}=0\)
Right limit at \(x=\frac{2}{3} is 3 \times \frac{2}{3}-2=0\)
\(f\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)=2-3 \times \frac{2}{3}=0\)
since, Left limit = Right limit \(=f\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)\)
Function is continuous at \(\frac{2}{3}\)
y is therefore continuous \(\forall x \in R\)
Now since \(2-3 x\) and \(3 x-2\) are polynomials,they are differentiable.
only concern is at \(x =\frac{2}{3}\)
Now, at \(x=\frac{2}{3}\), L D= Left derivative =-3
R D= Right derivative =+3
\(LD \neq RD\)
\(\therefore\) The function y is not differentiable at
\(x=\frac{2}{3}\)
So, we can say that y is differential \(\forall \bar{x} \in R\), except at \(x=\frac{2}{3}\)

questions.question:
The parabolic arc \(y=\sqrt{x}, 1\leq x\leq 2\)

questions.question: The standard deviation of a uniformly distributed random variable between 0 and 1 is
questions.explanation:
For uniformly distributed random variable \(P(x)=P\)
\(P(v)=\) probability density function
\[\begin{array}{c} \int_{E\left(x^{2}\right) \text{mean }=}^{1} x P(x) d x \quad \int_{0}^{1} x p d x \\ =\frac{P\left[x^{2} / 2\right]_{0}^{1}}{P[x]_{0}^{1}}=\frac{1}{2} \\ \qquad \begin{aligned} \Rightarrow E\left(x^{2}\right)&=\frac{\int x^{2} P(x) d x}{\int P(x) d x}\\&=\frac{\int_{0}^{1} x^{2} p d x}{\int_{0}^{1} p d x}\\ &=\frac{p\left[x^{3} / 3\right]_{0}^{1}}{p[x]_{0}^{1}} \\ &=\frac{p(1 / 3-0)}{p(1-0)} \end{aligned} \\ \qquad \begin{aligned} \text { variance } \sigma^{2} &=E\left(x^{2}\right)-(E(x))^{2} \\ &=\frac{1}{3}-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{2}\\ &=\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{12} \end{aligned} \end{array}\]
Standard deviation \(\sigma=\frac{1}{\sqrt{12}}\)

Alternate
\(^{\prime} x^{\prime} \; \text{defined on} \; [0,1]\)
Variance \(\quad U(x)=\frac{(b-a)^{2}}{12}=\frac{(1-0)^{2}}{12}\)
\(\therefore\) Standard deviation
\(\sigma=\frac{1}{\sqrt{12}}\)

 and \(x^{2}=4y\)

\(\text{Curve 2:} x^{2}=4 y\)
Intersection points of curve 1 and 2

\(then \quad x=4 \quad x=0\)
Therefore intersection point are A(4,4) and 0(0,0)

questions.subject: engineering-mathematics
questions.question:
The distance between the origin and the point nearest to it on the surface \(z^{2}=1+xy\)
 is
questions.explanation:
Let the point be the(x,y,z)

The distance between two given coordinates is given as
\[\begin{aligned} D^{2} &=\sqrt{(x-0)^{2}+(y-0)^{2}-(z-0)^{2}} \\ D^{2} &=x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2} \\ \text { given } z^{2} &=1+x y \\ D^{2} &=x^{2}+y^{2}+1+x y \end{aligned}\]
Let \(D^{2}=U\)
\(U=x^{2}+y^{2}+1+x y\)
For minimum or nearest distance
\[\begin{aligned} p &=\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=0 \\ \Rightarrow 2x+y &=0 &... i \\ \Rightarrow \quad q &=\frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=0 \\ &=2y+x=0&... ii \end{aligned}\]
By solving equation (i) and (ii)
\[\begin{aligned} &x=0\\ &y=0\\ &z=1\\ &\begin{aligned} r &=\frac{\partial^{2} v}{\partial x^{2}}=2 \\ t &=\frac{\partial^{2} v}{\partial y^{2}}=2 \\ s &=\frac{\partial^{2} u}{\partial x \partial y}=1 \\ r t-s^{2} &=2 \times 2-1^{2}=3 \\ r t-s^{2} &>0 \\r &>0 \end{aligned} \end{aligned}\]
\(\therefore\) distance is minimum.
Hence the distance should be
\(D=\sqrt{(0-0)^{2}+(0-0)^{2}-(1-0)^{2}}\)
\(D=1 \mathrm{m}\)

questions.subject: engineering-mathematics
questions.question: A path AB in the form of one quarter of a circle of unit radius is shown in the figure. Integration of \((x+y)^{2}\) on path AB traversed in a counter-clockwise sense is
questions.explanation:
Path AB:
\[\begin{aligned} x^{2}+y^{2} &=1 \\ x &=\cos \theta \\ y &=\sin \theta \end{aligned}\]
Along path AB \(\theta\) varies from \(0^{\circ} \; \text { to } \; 90^{\circ}[0 \text { to } \pi / 2]\)
\(\int_{\text {Path } A B}(x+y)^{2}(r d \theta)\)
\(=\int_{0}^{\pi / 2}(\cos \theta+\sin \theta)^{2} 1 \cdot d \theta\)
\(=\int_{0}^{\pi / 2}\left(\sin ^{2} \theta+\cos ^{2} \theta+2 \sin \theta \cos \theta\right) d \theta\)
\(=\int_{0}^{\pi / 2}(1+\sin 2 \theta) d \theta\)
\(=\theta+\left.\frac{(-\cos 2 \theta)}{2}\right|_{0} ^{\pi / 2}\)
\(=\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\left[\cos 2 \frac{\pi}{2}-\cos 0\right]\)
\(=\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{1}{2}[-1-1]=\frac{\pi}{2}+1\)

questions.question:
The solution of \(x\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}+y=x^{4}\)
  with the condition \(y(1)=\frac{6}{5}\)
 is
questions.explanation:
Given differential equation is
\[\begin{aligned} x \frac{d y}{d x}+y &=x^{4} \\ \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}+\left(\frac{1}{x}\right) y &=x^{3} \end{aligned}\]
Standard form
\(\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x}+P y=Q\)
where P and Q function of x only and solution is given by
\(y(\text { I.F. })=\int Q \cdot(I F .) d x+C\)
where, integrating factor (I.F.)\(=e^{\int P d x}\)
\(\text{Here} \quad P =\frac{1}{x} \text { and } Q=x^{3}\)
\(\text { I.F. } =e^{\int \frac{1}{x} d x}=e^{\ln x}=x\)
Solution \(\quad y(x)=\int x^{3} \cdot x d x+c\)
\(y x=\frac{x^{5}}{5}+c\)
given condition
\(y(1)=\frac{6}{5}\)
means at \(x=1 ; y=\frac{6}{5}\)
\(\Rightarrow \quad \frac{6}{5} \times 1=\frac{1}{5}+c\)
\(\Rightarrow \quad c=\frac{6}{5}-\frac{1}{5}=1\)
Therefore \(y x=\frac{x^{5}}{5}+1\)
\(\Rightarrow \quad y=\frac{x^{4}}{5}+\frac{1}{x}\)

An analytic function of a Complex Variables z = x + iy is expressed as \(f(z)=u(x,y)+iv(x,y)\)
 where \(i=\sqrt{-1}\). If u = xy, the expression for v should be
questions.explanation:
\[\begin{aligned} u &=x y \\ u_{x} &=\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=y \\ u_{y} &=\frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=x \\ f(z) &=u(x, y)+i v(x, y) \\ f^{\prime}(z) &=u_{x}+i v_{x}=v_{y}-i u_{y} \end{aligned}\]
Cauchy Riemann Equation
\[\begin{aligned} u_{x} &=v_{y} \\ v_{x} &=-u_{y} \\ f^{\prime}(z) &=u_{x}-i u_{y} \\ f^{\prime}(z) &=y-i x \\ \text{Put x=z and y}&=0\\ f^{\prime}(z) &=0-i z \\ f(z) &=\int(-i z) d z \\ f(z) &=-i \frac{z^{2}}{2}+c_{1}+i c_{2} \\ c_{1} &=0(\text { constant in real part }) \\ f(z) &=\frac{-i z^{2}}{2}+i c_{2} \\ &=\frac{-i(x+i y)^{2}}{2}+i c_{2} \\ f(z) &=x y+\frac{i\left(y^{2}-x^{2}\right)}{2}+i c_{2} \\ f(z) &=u(x, y)+i v(x, y) \end{aligned}\]
Comparing imaginary part
\[\begin{aligned} v &=\frac{y^{2}-x^{2}}{2}+c_{2} \\ &=\frac{y^{2}-x^{2}}{2}+k \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: engineering-mathematics
questions.question: If three coins are tossed simultaneously, the probability of getting at least one head
questions.explanation:
Three coins are tossed simultaneously, the total
number of ways \(=2^{3}=8\)
Number of ways to get all tails = 1
\(Probability to get all tails\)
\(=\frac{\text { Number of ways for tails }}{\text { Total number of ways }}=\frac{1}{8}\)
Therefore probability to get at least one head is
\(=1-\frac{1}{8}=\frac{7}{8}\)
or, Total number of ways with at least one head is
\[\left.\begin{matrix} & &\left.\begin{array}{lll} H & T & T \\ T & H & T \\ T & T & H \end{array} \right] \\ &&\left.\begin{array}{lll} H & T & T \\ T & H & T \\ T & T & H \end{array} \right] \\ &&\left.\begin{array}{lll} H & H & H \end{array} \right] \end{matrix}\right\}\]
Therefore probability to get at least one head \(=\frac{7}{8}\)

questions.subject: engineering-mathematics
questions.question:
The inverse Laplace transform of \(\frac{1}{(s^{2}+s)}\)
 is
questions.explanation:
\[\begin{aligned} L^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{s^{2}+s}\right) &=? \\ \frac{1}{s^{2}+s} &=\frac{1}{s(s+1)}=\frac{1}{s}-\frac{1}{s+1} \\ L^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{s^{2}+s}\right) &=L^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{s}\right)--L^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{s+1}\right) \\ &=1-e^{-t} \end{aligned}\]
[Using standard formulae]
Standard formula:
\[\begin{aligned} L^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{s}\right) &=1 \\ L^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{s+a}\right) &=e^{-a t} \\ L^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{s-a}\right) &=e^{a t} \end{aligned}\]

\(\vec{f}=\left[f_{1} \hat{i}+f_{2} \hat{j}+f_{3} \hat{k}\right]\)
\[\begin{aligned}&\text{Divergence of vector field} \vec{f}=\nabla \cdot \vec{f} \\ &\text{Div}(f)=\left(i \frac{\partial}{\partial x}+\hat{j} \frac{\partial}{\partial y}+\hat{k} \frac{\partial}{\partial z}\right) \cdot\left(t_{1} \hat{i}+f_{2} \hat{j}+f_{3} \hat{k}\right) \\ &\text{Div}(f)=\frac{\partial f_{1}}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial f_{2}}{\partial y}+\frac{\partial f_{3}}{\partial z} \\ &\text{Div}(f)=\frac{\partial}{\partial x}[3 x z]+\frac{\partial}{\partial y}[2 x y]+\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\left[-2 y z^{2}\right] \\ &\text{Div}(f)=3 z+2 x-2 z y \\ &\text{Div}(f)|_{(1,1,1)}=3(1)+2(1)-2(1)(1)=3 \end{aligned}\]

questions.question:
For a matrix \[[M]=\begin{bmatrix} \frac{3}{5} & \frac{4}{5}\\ x & \frac{3}{5} \end{bmatrix}\]
  the transpose of the matrix is equal to the inverse of the matrix \([M]^{T}= [M]^{-1}\). The value of x is given by
questions.explanation:
\(\text{If }\quad A^{T}=A^{-1}\)
then A is orthogonal matrix.
Therefore \(A . A^{-1}=A^{-1} A=I\)
\(\text{and }A^{T} A=A A^{T}=I\)
since \(\mathrm{M}\) is orthogonal matrix
\(M^{T} M=I\)
\[=\left[\begin{array}{cc}\frac{3}{5} & x \\ \frac{4}{5} & \frac{3}{5}\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{cc}\frac{3}{5} & \frac{4}{5} \\ x & \frac{3}{5}\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{cc}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{array}\right]\]
\[\left[\begin{aligned} \left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^{2}+x^{2} \quad\left(\frac{3}{5} \cdot \frac{4}{5}\right)+\frac{3}{5} x \\ \left(\frac{4}{5} \cdot \frac{3}{5}\right)+\frac{3}{5} \cdot x\left(\frac{4}{5}\right)^{2}+\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^{2} \end{aligned} \right]\]
\[=\left[\begin{array}{cc}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{array}\right] \Rightarrow \text{Compare both sides} a_{12}\]
\(a_{12}=\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)\left(\frac{4}{5}\right)+\left(\frac{3}{5}\right) x=0\)
\(\Rightarrow \quad \frac{3}{5} x=-\frac{3}{5} \cdot \frac{4}{5}\)
\(\Rightarrow x=-\frac{4}{5}\)

\[\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \qquad D&=-1,-1 \\ \therefore \qquad y&=\left(C_{1}+C_{2} x\right) e^{-x} \\ \Rightarrow \qquad 0&=\left(C_{1}+C_{2}(0)\right) e^{-0} \\ \Rightarrow \qquad C_{1}&=0\\ 0 &=\left(C_{1}+C_{2}\right) e^{-1} \\ \Rightarrow \qquad C_{1}+C_{2}&=0 \\ \Rightarrow \qquad C_{2}&=0 \\ \therefore \qquad y(0.5)&=0 \end{aligned}\]

questions.question: Let \(f=y^x\). What is \(\frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x\partial y}\) at x=2, y=1?
questions.explanation: \[\begin{aligned} f &=y^{x} \\ \ln f &=x \ln y \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{f} \frac{\partial f}{\partial y} &=\frac{x}{y} \\ \Rightarrow \frac{\partial f}{\partial y} &=y^{x}\left(\frac{x}{y}\right)=y^{x-1} x \\ \Rightarrow \frac{\partial^{2} f}{\partial x \partial y}&=\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(y^{x-1} x\right)\\ &=y^{x-1}+x y^{x-1} \ln y \\ &=1^{(2-1)}(1+2 \cdot \ln 1)=1 \end{aligned}\]

questions.question: The Eigenvectors of the matrix \[\begin{bmatrix} 1 &2 \\ 0& 2 \end{bmatrix}\] are written in the form \[\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ a \end{bmatrix}\] and \[\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ b \end{bmatrix}\]. What is a + b?
questions.explanation:
\[\left|\begin{array}{cc}(1-\lambda) & 2 \\ 0 & (2-\lambda)\end{array}\right|=0\]
\(\Rightarrow \qquad(1-\lambda)(2-\lambda)=0\)
\(\therefore \lambda=1,2\)
Putting the value of \(\lambda=1\)
\[\Rightarrow \qquad\left[\begin{array}{ll}0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}1 \\ a\end{array}\right]=0\]
\(\Rightarrow \qquad a=0\)
putting the value of \(\lambda=2\)
\[\begin{aligned}\left[\begin{array}{cc}-1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}1 \\ b\end{array}\right] &=0 \\ \Rightarrow \qquad b &=\frac{1}{2} \end{aligned}\]
\(\therefore \qquad a+b=\frac{1}{2}\)

questions.question:
Consider a continuous random variable with probability density function
\(f(t)= 1+t\) for \(-1\leq t \leq 0\)
\(f(t)= 1-t\) for \(0\leq t \leq 1\)
The standard deviation of the random variable is:
questions.explanation:
Mean \((\bar{t})=\int_{-1}^{\infty} t \cdot f(t) \cdot d t\)
\(\quad=\int_{-1}^{0} t(1+t) d t+\int_{0}^{1} t(1-t) d t\)
\(\quad=\left[\frac{t^{2}}{2}+\frac{t^{3}}{3}\right]_{-1}^{0}+\left[\frac{t^{2}}{2}-\frac{t^{3}}{3}\right]_{0}^{1}\)
\(\quad=-\left[\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{3}\right]+\left[\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{3}\right]\)
\(=-\left[\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{6}\right]=0\)
Variance \(=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}(t-\bar{t})^{2} f(t) d t\)
\(=\int_{-1}^{0} t^{2}(1+t) \cdot d t+\int_{0}^{1} t^{2}(1-t) d t\)
\(=\int_{-1}^{0}\left(t^{2}+t^{3}\right) \cdot d t+\int_{0}^{1} t^{2}(1-t) d t\)
\(=\left[\frac{t^{3}}{3}+\frac{t^{4}}{4}\right]_{-1}^{0}+\left[\frac{t^{3}}{3}-\frac{t^{4}}{4}\right]_{0}^{1}\)
\(=\frac{1}{12}+\frac{1}{12}=\frac{1}{6}\)
Standard deviation
\(=\sqrt{\text { variance }}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\)

questions.question:
Multiplication of matrices E and F is G. Matrices E and G are
\[E=\begin{bmatrix} \cos \theta & -\sin \theta & 0\\ \sin \theta & \cos \theta & 0\\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\] and \[G=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0\\ 0 & 1 & 0\\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\]
What is the matrix F?
questions.explanation:
\[E=\left[\begin{array}{ccc} \cos \theta & -\sin \theta & 0 \\ \sin \theta & \cos \theta & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right]\]
\[\text{and} G=\left[\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right]\]
The according to problem
\(E \times F=G\)
\[\text{or} \left[\begin{array}{ccc}\cos \theta & \sin \theta & 0 \\ -\sin \theta & \cos \theta & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{array}\right] \times F=\left[\begin{array}{ccc}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{array}\right]\]
Hence we see that product of \((E \times F)\) is unit matrix
so F will be the inverse of E
\[F=E^{-1}=\left[\begin{array}{ccc}\cos \theta & \sin \theta & 0 \\ -\sin \theta & \cos \theta & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{array}\right]\]

questions.question:
The vector field \(\vec{F}=x\vec{i}-y\vec{j}\)
 (where \(\vec{i}\)
 and \(\vec{j}\)
 are unit vectors )  is
questions.explanation:
\(\vec{F}=x\hat{i}-y\hat{j}\)
For divergence
Grade \(\vec{F}=\Delta \cdot \vec{F}\)
\(\;\;=\left ( \hat{i}\frac{\partial }{\partial x}+\hat{j}\frac{\partial }{\partial y} +\hat{k}\frac{\partial }{\partial z}\right )\cdot (x\hat{i}-y\hat{j})\)
\(\;\;=1-1=0\)
Hence vector field is divergence free.
For irrotation
Curl \(\vec{F}=\Delta \times \vec{F}\)
\(\;\;=\left ( \hat{i}\frac{\partial }{\partial x}+\hat{j}\frac{\partial }{\partial y} +\hat{k}\frac{\partial }{\partial z}\right )\times (x\hat{i}-y\hat{j})\)
\[\;\;=\begin{vmatrix} i & j & k\\ \frac{\partial }{\partial x}& \frac{\partial }{\partial y} & \frac{\partial }{\partial z}\\ x& -y & 0 \end{vmatrix}\]
\(\;\;=\hat{i}(0-0)-\hat{j}(0-0)+\hat{k}(0-0)=0\)
Hence vector field is irrotational

questions.subject: engineering-mathematics
questions.question:
Consider the system of simultaneous equation
\(x+2y+z=6\)
\(2x+y+2z=6\)
\(x+y+z=5\)
This system has
questions.explanation:
Given equation are
\[\begin{array}{r} x+2 y+z=6 \\ 2 x+y+2 z=6 \\ x+y+z=5 \end{array}\]
Given system can be written as
\[\left[\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l} x \\ y \\ z \end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{l} 6 \\ 6 \\ 5 \end{array}\right]\]
Applying row operation
\[\begin{array}{l} R_{2} \rightarrow R_{2}-2 R_{1}, R_{3} \rightarrow R_{3}-R_{1} \\ {\left[\begin{array}{ccc} 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l} x \\ y \\ z \end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{c} 6 \\ -6 \\ -1 \end{array}\right]} \end{array}\]
\(\text{and applying} R_{3} \rightarrow 3 R_{3}-R_{2}\)
\[\left[\begin{array}{ccc} 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l} x \\ y \\ z \end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{c} 6 \\ -6 \\ 3 \end{array}\right]\]
since the rank of coefficient matrix is 2 and rank of argument matrix is 3, which are not equal. Hence, system has no solution.

 the Eigen values are
questions.explanation:
\[\small A=\left[\begin{array}{ll}4 & 1 \\ 1 & 4\end{array}\right]\]
\(\text{Now }\quad|A-\lambda I|=0\)
\(\text{where} \quad \lambda= \text{ eigen value}\)
\[\therefore \quad\left|\begin{array}{cc}4-\lambda & 1 \\ 1 & 4-\lambda \\ (4-\lambda)^{2}-1 & =0\end{array}\right|=0\]
\(\text{or,} \quad(4-\lambda)^{2}-(1)^{2}=0\)
\(\text{or,} (4-\lambda+1)(4-\lambda-1)=0\)
\(\text{or,} \quad(5-\lambda)(3-\lambda)=0\)
\(\therefore \quad \lambda=3,5\)
